newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA COTTON MIXED ON SHORT SUPPLY, PROFIT-TAKING.
newsitem.headline: INDIA COTTON MIXED ON SHORT SUPPLY, PROFIT-TAKING.

text.p: Gujarat cotton extended gains while Punjab varieties suffered a setback on the local market on Friday, dealers said.
Gujarat varieties lifted further on the back of thin supplies and shortage of ready stock, while Punjab cotton fell on profit-taking by the speculators.
"Punjab varieties remained firm in the recent days purely on speculative interest which petered out today," one broker said.

In the spot deals Gujarat Kalyan rose by 200 rupees at 14,200/14,900 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while Kala-ginned rose by 100/200 rupees at 12,500 rupees and Wagad at 200/300 rupees at 13,300 rupees per candy.
In the Punjab segment saw-ginned cotton slid by 5 rupees at 1,825/1,870 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Bengal-deshi fell 10 rupees at 1,060/1,110 rupees per maund.
Traders reported the commencement of new crop arrivals in southern India and particularly in Karnataka. In spot deals new crop LRA cotton was quoted at 21,200/21,500 rupees per candy.
